editorial:
Imagine waking up with no memory of the night before, only to find out a monster is on the loose and all the clues point straight to you. That is the wild ride you get with Thomas Krömer. He is just a guy trying to solve a series of scary, wolf-like murders, but the more he digs, the more he realizes he might be the beast. The vibe is creepy and tense, especially when things get personal and his own grandmother is attacked in her cute little house in the woods. It feels like a dark mystery where you are constantly guessing if the main character is actually a killer or just a victim of a huge prank.

You will love how the tension builds as the full moon gets closer. The acting is solid and the twisty plot keeps you on your toes, even if some of the older effects feel a bit dated. It is a great pick for a late-night movie marathon with friends. If you want the best experience, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for those crisp night shots, or just rent it on Apple TV for a quick watch. If you are a big horror fan, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is definitely the way to go.
endingExplained: The big twist reveals that Thomas is not actually a werewolf. He was being tricked by a sinister group that used drugs and hypnosis to make him believe he was changing. They wanted him to take the fall for the murders they committed. In the end, the real killers are exposed, and Thomas manages to fight back and survive. He clears his name just as the moon reaches its peak, proving he was innocent all along.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves creature features and psychological twists.
